title: Specific performance and adequacy of damages
shortTitle: Specific performance and adequacy of damages
summary: Specific performance is a court order requiring the promised performance. An injunction may similarly restrain conduct that violates a contractual obligation.
notes:
The assigned cases examine whether money would adequately compensate the injured party and whether a court can administer the requested order. Morris concerns a specially trained horse, Klein an aircraft for which substitutes were available, and Walgreen a lease restriction whose violation would cause difficult-to-measure competitive loss. The remedy depends on the transaction and equitable considerations; an enforceable contract does not automatically entitle its claimant to specific relief.

Morris uses the particular trained horse’s value to the plaintiff. The notes extend the inquiry to affection for a pet and the inability to obtain sufficient tomatoes at the needed time for a cannery. Uniqueness is relevant through difficulty of substitution, not only through a category label. Personal services present different concerns; a negative injunction against competing performance is distinct from an affirmative order to render services.
